What are the four types of AI agent loops?
:   The four loop types are: heartbeat loops (run continuously on a short interval), cron loops (scheduled at specific times like daily at 10am), hook loops (triggered by events like a PR push or CI failure), and goal loops (iterate until a success condition is met, then stop). Each fits different workflows.

How do subagents work inside agent loops?
:   Subagents separate the loop controller from the workers. The main loop agent decomposes a task, spawns specialized subagents in isolated worktrees, collects their results, and decides whether to continue or stop. # Loop Engineering: How to Build AI Agent Loops That Run Themselves

Published

The biggest shift in AI agent development in June 2026 is not a new model. It is a new way of using them. Loop engineering has become the dominant pattern for production agent workflows, replacing the manual prompt, wait, review cycle with autonomous systems that run themselves.

The core idea: you do not prompt the agent. You design the system that prompts the agent. The agent iterates until done, reports findings, and waits for the next trigger.

[...] ### The Explore-Narrow Loop

The agent explores multiple solution paths simultaneously (or sequentially), then narrows to the most promising one based on intermediate results.

When to use: Debugging unknown errors, exploring unfamiliar APIs, optimizing performance. Situations where you don’t know the right approach upfront.

Watch out for: Context explosion. Running multiple paths in parallel is expensive. Pruning early and often is essential.

### The Human-in-the-Loop

Technically a loop variant — the agent runs until it needs clarification or hits an ambiguity, pauses for human input, then continues. [...] AI coding tools have matured through several phases. First came autocomplete (GitHub Copilot’s original form). Then came inline chat (ask a question, get a code snippet). Now, the state of the art is full coding agents that operate autonomously over long tasks.

Tools like Claude Code, Devin, and OpenAI’s Codex Agent all rely on loop engineering as their core operating model. The agent is given a task, a codebase, and a set of tools — and then it loops: reading files, writing code, running tests, reading errors, revising, repeating.

# A Doer And Judge Strengthen Every AI Agent Loop

Every reliable AI Agent Loop needs one agent that performs the task and another agent that checks the result.

The first agent is the doer, which may write the article, build the page, research the market, or repair the code.

The second agent acts as the judge and compares the output against the goal you defined.

Separating those responsibilities matters because creators are often too close to their own work to grade it honestly.

An agent that has just completed a task may assume the result is acceptable because it followed its own reasoning.

A separate judge has less attachment to the original approach and can identify gaps more clearly.

The judge does not always need to be more intelligent than the builder. [...] Maximum rounds can also prevent the system from spending too much time or money chasing a perfect result.

When the limit is reached, the loop can return the best version alongside the remaining issues.

Good boundaries make autonomous work more predictable because the agent understands both the destination and the stopping point.

# Hermes And Claude Code Power The AI Agent Loop

Hermes can support an AI Agent Loop by giving separate agent profiles different responsibilities inside one workflow.

A builder profile can create the first version while an editor improves clarity, structure, and consistency.

Another profile can act as the judge and reject work that fails the quality gate.
